caption:
Give an input a value without an onChange in your machine coding round, and the search box ignores every key the interviewer presses.

Look at the card. value={q} tells React that state owns this text. After every keystroke React puts the input back to q. Nothing ever changes q, so it stays empty.

React even warns in the console: a value prop without an onChange handler renders a read-only field.

Two ways out:
value plus onChange, when you need the text in state (filtering as you type).
defaultValue, when you only read it on submit.

Pick one per input. Don't mix them.

Source: react.dev, <input> (controlling an input with a state variable).
